answer: Every claim carries its own ridge to climb: before filing, the claimant must solve a fresh computation bound to that claim's exact contents — a puzzle taking about an hour on ordinary hardware. The desk checks the solution within a day; a claim with a missing or copied solution is voided. One honest user climbs one ridge, while 1,000 fakes would need 1,000 hours of computing — a gap near 1,000 to 1. When one operator tried to wander a thousand fresh identities past the harbor gate, the desk found the same copied solution on every claim and turned them all away.
